affected_predicate.description: Every file whose original name begins with bid_ is renamed to bid_{sequence}.{original_extension}, with sequence numbers assigned from earliest to latest date.

competing_trace_defects.description: The rename input supplied the full name bid_1.txt while the dialog retained the original extension, visibly producing bid_1.txt.txt before the reuse target.

The agent selected the Aug 18 bid_food_supplier_quote.txt as sequence 1 even though the visible Aug 11 bid_menu_design_contract.pdf was earlier, independently conflicting with earliest-to-latest numbering.
A normal click on bid_food_supplier_quote.txt opened the Android chooser instead of entering rename selection; the agent then returned to Files.

chains.rationale: At reuse step 13, the agent explicitly repeated the false premise that an extra extension had been deleted and clicked inside the filename field without performing a text-deletion action. Steps 14-19 alternate similarly ineffective field and dialog clicks while bid_1.txt.txt remains visible, forming an observed loop. Step 19 exits the dialog and visibly returns to a list where bid_food_supplier_quote.txt is still unchanged; step 20 switches to the other bid_ file, interrupting rather than correcting the loop. Later visible list states also retain the original bid_ filenames, so the date-ordered renaming predicate is observably unsatisfied. This is a mechanism judgment only and does not assert causation or a hidden task outcome.

summary: The single frozen strict-MHR chain shows the reused false-completion claim bridging into repeated ineffective clicks on the duplicate-extension rename dialog. That loop is later interrupted by switching files, without visible correction; the supplied trace continues to show the original bid_ filenames. Independently observable prefix defects include incorrect date-order numbering, creation of the duplicate extension, and an unintended file-open detour.
